calls.headline: Goldman calls the pound 30% undervalued as Cairo rations its dollars
calls.body: Goldman Sachs says the pound trades more than 30% below fair value on a real effective exchange rate basis after October's slide past 56, up from 13–15% in June, and now sees the dollar at EGP 53 in three months, 52 in six and 50 in a year, keeping its buy call (a note reported by Asharq Bloomberg and EnterpriseAM). It estimates foreign holdings of local debt fell to about $20bn from about $30bn at the end of September. The same week, the Cabinet ordered three months of spending cuts across state bodies and made any spending with a foreign-currency component subject to Finance Ministry approval, coordinated with the central bank (Amwal Al Ghad, Middle East Monitor). The central bank's dollar rate closed Thursday at EGP 54.01, after six straight falls.
calls.view: Two things now push the same way: a large investor says the pound is cheap and pays well to hold, and the state is cutting its own demand for dollars. With October inflation at 12.0% against 26% one-year bills, the carry case holds even if the Fed hikes in December. The $10bn that already left is the warning: if regional news turns, the rest can leave fast. Banks gain most from steady rates and a firm pound; importers gain from cheaper dollars.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 56 before the end of November, or the week's bill auctions clear well below last week's yields as foreign demand fades.

calls.headline: Spending freeze and bigger export rebates: contractors lose, exporters gain
calls.line: The state is cutting its own bills and paying more for every dollar earned abroad.
calls.body: The decree cuts government electricity use by 20% and official fuel by at least 30%, freezes at least 20% of remaining goods-and-services allocations, slows fuel-hungry national projects and bars new projects this fiscal year; health, pensions, cash support and food subsidies are exempt. A revamped export rebate program raises support by an average of 35% from November shipments and pays half of sea and land freight to Africa, Latin America, Southeast Asia and Russia (EnterpriseAM, Masrawy); textiles, food, engineering, pharma, chemicals and building materials are covered, free zones are not. The budget sets aside EGP 48bn for export support this year against EGP 28bn paid out last year.
calls.view: Exporters with dollar sales and low free-zone exposure are the clearest winners: Elsewedy's cables, food exporters such as Edita, and building-material makers. Contractors that rely on state work lose new awards for the rest of the fiscal year; Orascom Construction is cushioned by mostly foreign revenue. For the pound, both steps cut the need for dollars.
calls.wrong: Elsewedy falls back below EGP 105 by the end of November, about 10% under Thursday's close, as the rebate boost fails to show.

calls.headline: Orascom allots 97.2 million new shares to OCI, nearly doubling its count
calls.line: The OCI merger is close to done, and new shares reach OCI's holders in December.
calls.body: Orascom Construction's board approved raising capital to $207.4m from $110.2m by issuing 97.2 million new $1 shares to OCI N.V., completing January's shareholder approval, according to its filing to the exchange (Cairo24). The company targets November 24 to issue and list the new shares on the EGX and the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange, with crediting to OCI's holders from about December 8 and completion in December (Arab Finance). OCI's holders receive 0.4634 Orascom shares for each OCI share, ending with about 47% of the group. The stock closed Thursday at EGP 810.02, up 88.4% this year.
calls.view: The deal turns Orascom into a bigger, Abu Dhabi-based infrastructure investor with OCI's cash, but OCI's holders are a broad European base that did not choose Orascom, and some will sell once shares land in December. Expect supply to cap the stock into year-end even if the combined group is worth more.
calls.wrong: Orascom closes above EGP 900 before December 15, which would show demand absorbing the new shares.

calls.headline: Results week: Juhayna, CIB and Telecom Egypt report after the rate hike
calls.line: The first company numbers since October's currency slide and the 100 basis point hike.
calls.body: Juhayna is expected to report on Monday, CIB on Wednesday and Telecom Egypt on Thursday before the open (newsletter calendar, TradingView). Telecom Egypt's chief executive, Tamer El-Mahdy, told Al Borsa the company targets about $500m of network investment over five years and that subsea cable revenue grew 31% last fiscal year; he also aims to lift subsea cables crossing Egypt to 28 by 2028 from 15 (Mangish). CIB closed at EGP 128.00 and Telecom Egypt at EGP 128.55, up 24.3% and 95.5% this year.
calls.view: CIB's margins should show the benefit of higher rates, with loan growth the swing factor. Telecom Egypt has dollar income from cables, but at nearly double January's price it needs a clear beat; capex guidance matters as much as profit. Juhayna's report is the test of volumes after price rises.
calls.wrong: CIB closes below EGP 118 or Telecom Egypt below EGP 115 in the two sessions after their results.

calls.headline: Suez revenue nearly doubles to $724m as Gulf risk flares again
calls.line: The canal's recovery is the pound's best new dollar source, and weekend Gulf attacks test it.
calls.body: Suez Canal revenue reached $724m in October, up 94% on a year earlier and the highest monthly total since the Red Sea crisis began, on about 1,500 transits, the canal authority said (EnterpriseAM); Egypt Today counted 1,490 ships, the most since October 2023. Over the weekend, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers hit mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz (IRNA via Asharq Al-Awsat), and the Houthis claimed missile and drone attacks on Riyadh airport and Aramco sites (Middle East Eye, ABC News). Neither claim has been independently confirmed.
calls.view: At October's pace the canal would earn about $8.7bn a year, against $4.8bn last fiscal year, a real support for the pound. Shipping lines return when the Red Sea looks safe; Houthi fire on Saudi Arabia, if it turns to ships, would reverse that quickly.
calls.wrong: Monthly canal revenue falls back below $550m in November or December, or Houthi attacks on shipping resume.

calls.headline: Tuesday's CPI decides whether a December Fed hike is locked in
calls.body: October consumer prices are due Tuesday at 8:30am New York time, with an early FactSet estimate of 3.9% a year, up from 3.7% (CNBC). They follow 165,000 new jobs in October against forecasts near 65,000–70,000, which pushed December hike odds to about 77–80% on CME FedWatch and the 10-year Treasury yield to 4.86%. The VIX closed Friday at 25.64 (Cboe). Producer prices follow on Friday, and New York Fed President John Williams speaks Thursday.
calls.view: A hike is the base case; the question is whether more follow. A print at or above 3.9% keeps yields high and weighs on the most expensive stocks, growth and 40-times-earnings defensives alike, while helping bank margins. A soft print below about 3.6% would spark a relief rally led by chips. With the VIX above 25, the move either way will be large.
calls.wrong: CPI comes in under 3.6% and the 10-year yield falls below 4.60% by Friday.

calls.headline: Berkshire buys back a record $9.6bn as operating profit slips 5.8%
calls.line: Greg Abel's first big capital call is on Berkshire's own shares.
calls.body: Berkshire Hathaway's operating earnings fell 5.8% to $12.7bn in the third quarter as insurance underwriting income dropped (Bloomberg), and net income fell 28% as investment gains shrank (WSJ). It bought back a record $9.6bn of its own stock while chief executive Greg Abel was a net seller of other stocks (FT). Class B shares closed Friday at $571.06, up 13.6% this year and close to their 52-week high.
calls.view: Buybacks at about 1.6 times book say management thinks the stock is cheap, and they put a floor under it in a weak market; but the earnings fall shows insurance profits have peaked for now. Berkshire stays a steady holder rather than a growth story.
calls.wrong: Berkshire Class B closes below $530 by the end of November despite the buyback.

calls.headline: Nvidia's chief faces spy questions a week before results
calls.line: A political cloud over Nvidia's China dealings adds risk to the results that set the AI mood.
calls.body: The FT reported that the US government believes Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based customer Megaspeed whom US intelligence considers a recruit of China's Ministry of State Security; Bloomberg relayed a New York Times report along the same lines. Three House Republican committee chairs asked Huang to a closed-door briefing on November 18 (CNBC). Nvidia says its chief meets thousands of customers a year, and no one has been charged. Nvidia rose 2.8% to $186.64 on Friday; its results are expected on November 17.
calls.view: The story is unlikely to change Nvidia's numbers but it can change Washington's appetite for its China sales, the swing factor in guidance. Combined with Microsoft's pullback from rented capacity, it keeps chips under pressure into results, as the desk's open view expects.
calls.wrong: Nvidia closes above $210 before its results.

calls.headline: Weekend Gulf attacks test oil's 13% weekly fall
calls.line: Brent's drop priced a deal with Iran; the weekend brought mines in Hormuz and Houthi claims on Aramco.
calls.body: Brent settled at $98.32 on Friday after its steepest weekly fall since 2020 on bets of a US-Iran deal. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers hit mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on an "unauthorized route" (IRNA via Asharq Al-Awsat), and the Houthis claimed missile and drone attacks on Riyadh airport and Aramco sites in Khurais (Middle East Eye); Saudi Arabia reported no damage and neither claim has been confirmed. Qatar said US-Iran talks are still alive. Exxon closed Friday at $165.87, up 37.8% this year.
calls.view: Monday's open will show how much risk the market adds back; unconfirmed claims tend to fade unless ships or Saudi output are hit. The desk keeps its view that Brent stays below $105 while talks continue, at low confidence. Energy stocks are the hedge if it fails.

news.headline: Houthis claim missile and drone strikes on Riyadh airport and Aramco
news.text: Six operations were claimed; Saudi Arabia reported no damage.

news.headline: US disables an 11th ship trying to breach the Iran blockade
news.text: Central Command also set up Task Force Iron Gate to block Iran's land routes for weapons.

news.headline: Suez revenue hits $724m in October as container lines return
news.text: Up 94% on a year earlier; the highest monthly total since the Red Sea crisis began.
